stdout:
I've verified everything in the snapshot. Here's the full picture.

## Summary

**CVE-2024-39338 (GHSA-8hc4-vh64-cxmj) is genuinely fixed in axios v1.7.4, which was released today (2024-08-13).** If a scanner is still flagging v1.7.4, that is almost certainly a stale-database false positive or a lockfile still resolving an older version — not a real vulnerability in 1.7.4.

## What I verified in this snapshot

- **The vulnerability**: reported in issue #6463 (2024-06-24). On the server side, axios since v1.3.2 resolved protocol-relative URLs (`//attacker.com`) against `http://localhost`, so a request like `axios.get('/' + userId)` with `userId = '/google.com'` escaped the configured `baseURL` entirely — an SSRF vector. Affected range per the GitHub advisory: **1.3.2 ≤ axios ≤ 1.7.3**.
- **The fix**: PR #6539 (commit `07a661a`) plus a follow-up correction in PR #6543 (commit `6b6b605`), both merged today, released as **v1.7.4** (release PR #6544, changelog confirms "fix(sec): CVE-2024-39338"). The fix is visible in the code: `lib/adapters/http.js:232` now does `new URL(fullPath, utils.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined)` — in Node there is no longer a `http://localhost` fallback base, so a protocol-relative URL throws `ERR_INVALID_URL` instead of silently resolving to an arbitrary host. Browser behavior is unchanged.
- **The advisory** (GHSA-8hc4-vh64-cxmj, published 2024-08-12, HIGH severity) already lists `fixed: 1.7.4` with `last_known_affected: <= 1.7.3`.

## Why your scanner still flags v1.7.4, and what to do

1. **Scanner database lag.** v1.7.4 shipped only hours ago today; Snyk, `npm audit`, and similar tools were flagging the package yesterday with "no patch available" (see issues #6540, #6541, and comments on #6463). Their databases may not yet reflect the 1.7.4 fix line. Refresh/re-run the scan, and if it persists, report the false positive to the scanner vendor — the GitHub Advisory is the authoritative source and it marks 1.7.4 as fixed.
2. **Check what version is actually resolved.** A transitive dependency may still pin axios ≤1.7.3 even after you upgrade your direct dependency. Inspect your lockfile (`npm ls axios`) and force the version if needed via npm `overrides` / yarn `resolutions`.
3. **Make sure it's the same CVE.** Confirm the scanner finding is CVE-2024-39338 and not a different axios advisory.

## Workaround if you cannot upgrade

The vulnerability only triggers when attacker-controlled input reaches the request URL/path in a server-side context. Until you can move to 1.7.4:

- Validate or encode user input interpolated into URLs (e.g., `encodeURIComponent(userId)`), and reject any constructed path that begins with `//`.
- Equivalently, add a request interceptor that throws when `config.url` matches `/^\/\//` while a `baseURL` is set.

But upgrading to **1.7.4** is the real fix and is available as of today.
